chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: Whoever humiliates a friend of Mine, he has prepared himself for war with Me, and I am the quickest of things to aiding My friends.'

key_terms.أَرْصَدَ: He prepared or laid wait (for war)
key_terms.أَوْلِيَائِي: My friends (plural of wali, referring to those close to God)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when Allah says He is quick to help His friends?
ai.summary: This Qudsi hadith from al-Kafi establishes the theological principle that insulting the awliya (friends of God) constitutes a direct declaration of war against Allah, reflecting the Shia concept of their spiritual authority. It underscores the divine promise of swift victory for the awliya, reinforcing the social imperative of respecting the righteous in both individual piety and communal identity.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhamad, from Ali Bin Al Nu’man, from Ibn Muskan, from Moalla Bin Khunays who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High is Saying: “The one who despises (hates) a friend of Mine<sup>azwj</sup>, so he has declared a war against Me<sup>azwj</sup> and I<sup>azwj</sup> am the Quickest to Helping My<sup>azwj</sup> friends”’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Nu’man from ibn Muskan from Mu’alla ibn Khunayth who has said the following:
“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘Allah, the Most Blessed, the Most High, says, ‘Whoever insults any of My friends has waged a war against Me. I am the quickest to support My friends.’”
